$schema-note: Layer table for the A1 layering lint (graph.mjs section 8, layering.mjs). Layer orders encode the plan (docs/plans/2026-11-15-workspace-restructure-plan.md) section 2 bottom-to-top stack; expected_back_edges holds the plan section 1 claim checks (module-prefix based, independent of layer order). Back-edge = source layer order LOWER than target layer order (graph.mjs DEVIATION 1) — a dependency pointing UP the stack. segment and route are ONE layer segment_route (order 4) until the owner's G1 decision; their mutual references are same-layer and hence never back-edges (with the merged layer the old segment/route cycle observation produces zero cycleEdges — intended). The modules alloc_core and registry (group-wiring mod.rs files that only re-export across several future-crate boundaries) are declared status "conduit": their OWN edges are never back-edges, while references THROUGH them resolve to the defining module in the graph and count against the DEFINING module's layer; a module mapped to no layer and not declared a conduit is itself a lint finding (unmapped).

conduits.note: group-wiring mod.rs files that only re-export across several future-crate boundaries (A0 report, Unmapped-layer modules). A1: the conduit's own re-export edges are never back-edges; references THROUGH it resolve to the defining module in the graph, so they are counted against the defining module's layer, not the conduit's.
